people.name: Salahuddin al-Ayyubi
facts: Kurdish-born founder of the Ayyubid dynasty, he ruled Egypt and Syria in the 12th century.
Recaptured Jerusalem from the Crusaders in 1187.
Respected even by his enemies for his mercy and chivalry.

people.name: Malala Yousafzai
facts: Pakistani activist who campaigns for every girl’s right to go to school.
Survived being shot by the Taliban in 2012 for speaking out about girls’ education.
Won the Nobel Peace Prize in 2014 at age 17, the youngest winner ever.

people.name: Mohamed Salah
facts: Egyptian forward who became a star at Liverpool FC.
Has won the Premier League Golden Boot as the league’s top scorer several times.
Known for celebrating goals with sujood, a prostration of thanks.

people.name: Al-Khwarizmi
facts: 9th-century Persian scholar who worked at the House of Wisdom in Baghdad.
His book on “al-jabr” gave us the word algebra.
The word algorithm comes from his name.

people.name: Zaha Hadid
facts: Iraqi-British architect famous for flowing, curved buildings.
In 2004 she became the first woman to win the Pritzker Prize, architecture’s top award.
Designed the London Aquatics Centre for the 2012 Olympics.

people.name: Malcolm X
facts: American minister and one of the most influential voices of the civil rights era.
After performing Hajj in 1964, he embraced Sunni Islam and took the name el-Hajj Malik el-Shabazz.
His life story, The Autobiography of Malcolm X, is still widely read.

people.name: Ibn Sina
facts: Persian scholar (980–1037), known in Europe as Avicenna.
Wrote The Canon of Medicine, used to teach doctors in Europe and the Middle East for centuries.
Also wrote on philosophy, astronomy and music.

people.name: Zohran Mamdani
facts: Born in Kampala, Uganda, and moved to New York City as a child.
Represented Queens in the New York State Assembly from 2021.
Elected mayor of New York City in 2025, the city’s first Muslim mayor.

people.name: Ibtihaj Muhammad
facts: American sabre fencer from New Jersey.
First American woman to compete at the Olympics wearing a hijab, at Rio 2016.
Won a bronze medal in team sabre, and Mattel made a Barbie doll in her likeness.

people.name: Ahmed Zewail
facts: Egyptian-American scientist and professor at Caltech.
Won the 1999 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for watching chemical reactions with ultrafast lasers.
Is often called the father of femtochemistry.

people.name: Muhammad Ali
facts: American boxer nicknamed “The Greatest”.
Won Olympic gold in 1960 and became world heavyweight champion three times.
Refused to fight in the Vietnam War because of his faith and lost his title for it.

people.name: Nadiya Hussain
facts: British baker who won The Great British Bake Off in 2015.
Baked the cake for Queen Elizabeth II’s 90th birthday.
Has hosted her own BBC cooking shows and written cookbooks and children’s books.

people.name: Ibn Battuta
facts: 14th-century Moroccan explorer from Tangier.
Travelled for about 30 years across Africa, the Middle East and Asia, further than Marco Polo.
His travel book, the Rihla, describes the places he visited.

people.name: Hamdi Ulukaya
facts: Born in Turkey, he moved to the United States to study English.
Founded Chobani, which became the best-selling Greek yogurt brand in the US.
Known for hiring refugees and giving his employees shares in the company.

people.name: Omar Suleiman
facts: American imam and scholar from New Orleans.
Founder and president of the Yaqeen Institute for Islamic Research.
Known for his lectures and his civil rights and interfaith work.

people.name: Anousheh Ansari
facts: Iranian-American engineer who co-founded a telecommunications company.
In 2006 she flew to the International Space Station, the first Muslim woman in space.
Her family sponsored the Ansari X Prize for private spaceflight.

people.name: Abdul Sattar Edhi
facts: Pakistani humanitarian (1928–2016).
Founded the Edhi Foundation, which runs one of the world’s largest volunteer ambulance services.
Lived very simply and spent his life helping the poor, orphans and the sick.

people.name: Riz Ahmed
facts: British actor and rapper with Pakistani heritage.
In 2017 he became the first Muslim to win an Emmy for a lead acting role.
Was nominated for the Best Actor Oscar for Sound of Metal.
